text: Coordinating Texas AQS ground-site measurements during the 2026 NOAA Houston field campaign, including online CIMS-Orbitrap characterization of gas-phase pollutants.
Guest speaker for BIMS 110: One Health in Action at Texas A&M University.
Presented real-time particle-phase PFAS detection at the 2025 AAAR Annual Meeting in Buffalo, chaired the Source Apportionment 4 session, and received an Early Career Researchers Travel Grant.
Coordinated aerosol mass spectrometer operation and data-analysis training at the Center for Atmospheric Chemistry and the Environment, Texas A&M University.
Guest speaker for BIMS 110: One Health in Action at Texas A&M University.
Joined Texas A&M University as a Postdoctoral Research Associate in Atmospheric Sciences.
Completed my Ph.D. in Environmental Science at Peking University.
Received the Peking University President’s Scholarship for Doctoral Students and the Challenge Cup May Fourth Youth Science Award, Grand Prize, in 2022.
Completed teaching assistant certification at Peking University with qualified standing.
Served as a technical instructor for the Environmental Monitoring Experiment Course at Peking University, teaching offline aerosol sampling and instrumentation in 2020 and 2021.
Teaching assistant for the graduate course Atmospheric Measurement Principles, Techniques, and Applications at Peking University.
